# zuspecial

<!-- badges: start -->
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/pedrobtz/zuspecial/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/pedrobtz/zuspecial/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
[![coverage](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pedrobtz/zuspecial/gh-pages/badges/coverage.svg)](https://github.com/pedrobtz/zuspecial/actions/workflows/coverage.yaml)
[![Lifecycle: experimental](https://img.shields.io/badge/lifecycle-experimental-orange.svg)](https://lifecycle.r-lib.org/articles/stages.html#experimental)
<!-- badges: end -->

## Overview

R's special functions are scattered. Base R has the gamma function and
Bessel functions of real argument; complex Bessel functions,
hypergeometric functions, elliptic integrals and the Lambert W function
each live in their own package, or in `gsl`, which needs the GNU Scientific
Library installed. And when a model is written in Python and checked in R,
or the other way round, two libraries that disagree in the last digits are
a needless source of doubt.

zuspecial gives R the special functions of
[`scipy.special`](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/special.html),
computed by the same C++ kernels:
[xsf](https://github.com/scipy/xsf), the library SciPy's special functions
are built from, at the commit SciPy 1.18.1 uses.

* **SciPy's values.** Each function is tested against
  [xsref](https://github.com/scipy/xsref)'s mpmath reference tables, under
  xsf's own tolerances, and against SciPy 1.18.1 itself, on Linux, macOS
  and Windows.
* **Real and complex arguments.** Bessel, Hankel, Airy, gamma, error,
  exponential-integral, hypergeometric and zeta functions take complex
  arguments where SciPy does.
* **SciPy's names and argument order.** `sc_jv(v, z)` is
  `scipy.special.jv(v, z)`, so code translates line by line.
* **Ordinary R functions.** Vectorised and recycled, `NA`-aware, keeping
  names and dimensions; floating-point conditions follow SciPy's
  `seterr()`, as warnings or errors when asked for.
* **A C interface.** Other packages can call the functions from compiled
  code through `LinkingTo: zuspecial`.

Nothing is needed at run time; Boost.Math headers, from the BH package,
are needed to build it.

## Installation

zuspecial is not on CRAN yet. Install the development version from GitHub
with:

``` r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("pedrobtz/zuspecial")
```

## Usage

```{r, message = FALSE}
library(zuspecial)
```

Functions are vectorised, and take complex arguments where SciPy does:

```{r}
sc_gamma(c(0.5, 5))
sc_gamma(1 + 1i)
```

Arguments come in SciPy's order, the order first for the Bessel functions,
where base R's `besselJ()` puts it second:

```{r}
sc_jv(2.5, 3)
besselJ(3, 2.5)
```

As in SciPy, the type of the argument picks the result: the Bessel
function of order 0.5 at -1 is `NaN` for a real `-1`, and a complex number
for `-1+0i`:

```{r}
sc_jv(0.5, -1)
sc_jv(0.5, -1 + 0i)
```

Poles, overflow and loss of precision are silent by default, as in SciPy,
and can be turned into warnings or errors:

```{r}
sc_gamma(-1)
sc_errstate(sc_gamma(-1), singular = "warn")
```

Functions that return several values in SciPy return a named list:

```{r}
str(sc_airy(1))
```

Every function is `sc_` followed by its name in `scipy.special`, the
alias SciPy's own documentation uses (`import scipy.special as sc`).

## Learn more

* [Translating from
  scipy.special](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zuspecial/articles/scipy.html):
  names, argument types, error handling, multi-output functions, the C
  interface, and the few places zuspecial differs.
* The [reference index](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zuspecial/reference/),
  by family.
* `zuspecial_info()` for the versions and the table of functions.

## Acknowledgements

The kernels are SciPy's [xsf](https://github.com/scipy/xsf), with its
bundled Cephes, AMOS, specfun, Faddeeva and qd code, and Boost.Math for
the functions SciPy evaluates with it. The reference values come from
[xsref](https://github.com/scipy/xsref). zuspecial is also checked against
the `gsl`, `Bessel`, `hypergeo`, `lamW`, `expint` and `Rmpfr` packages.
